Division explicitly rejects denominators containing zero; reciprocal endpoints are ordered correctly for either positive or negative denominators. Empty intersections, nonpositive logarithm arguments and negative square-root lower bounds throw and cannot certify a cell.

MPFR receives binary endpoints exactly and evaluates exp/log/sqrt with directed rounding before directed conversion back to double. Decimal input parsing is separately directed downward and upward, enclosing the specified real decimal value.

phi(z)=(1+z)log(1+z)-z decreases on(-1,0) and increases on(0,infinity). Endpoint hulls and the exact zero minimum on crossing intervals therefore enclose it; clipping a negative lower rounding artifact to zero uses a proved global lower bound.

First-order interval automatic differentiation uses the product and quotient rules with interval values and all nine parameter/time derivatives. For phi its derivative is log(1+z), including negative arguments above-1.

The entire functions cosh(sqrt(z)) and sinh(sqrt(z))/sqrt(z) have positive Taylor coefficients for z>=0; their derivatives are respectively half the second function and the explicitly evaluated third function.

For z<1e-8, retaining terms through degree8 leaves tails far below1e-80 for each function, including f1-prime. The f1-prime recurrence multiplies by z(n+1)/(n(2n+2)(2n+3)), matching its exact coefficients.

For larger z, the MPFR formulas account for cancellation in(cosh(sqrt(z))-sinh(sqrt(z))/sqrt(z))/(2z) with separately outward terms. Real fast spectra justify clipping squared gaps to the nonnegative domain.

295 primitive regression comparisons cover cancellation, subnormal binary values, exp/log/sqrt, zero and both sides of the1e-8 entire-function branch, phi across its minimum, and five invalid-domain rejections. These point checks supplement the analytic arithmetic argument.
reduction_and_spectrum: The model uses six independent physical coordinates: three positive gaps and three symmetric barrier excesses. Downward exp(-h) and upward exp(-h-(Ej-Ei)) satisfy detailed balance with exp(-Ei) exactly; column diagonals conserve mass.

For a zero-sum probability deviation, eliminate its fourth coordinate as minus the first three. A directed edge j-to-i contributes the reduced matrix(delta_ai-delta_aj)*(delta_bj if j<3 else-1); the code matches this convention.

The fixed near-eigenbasis is specified by exact decimals rather than assumed exact numerical eigenvectors. Interval Gaussian elimination encloses its inverse and rejects any pivot interval through zero.

Transforming each constant edge matrix before multiplying its uncertain rate retains cancellations without altering the mathematical reduced generator. The basis and inverse remain parameter independent.

Centered mean-value intersections for R, Gibbs coordinates and modal inputs use the original whole-box derivative enclosures and a recomputed point value. Omitting coordinate8 there is correct because these quantities do not depend on time.
The characteristic polynomial is det(xI-R) in scalar-plus-two-block form. Its derivative includes the block determinant and the two off-diagonal coupling derivatives with the correct signs.

Opposite endpoint polynomial signs and positive derivative on[-.015,-.001] establish one simple root for every parameter choice. Interval Newton intersections and the Schur-complement fixed-point equation both preserve every such root.

Implicit derivatives of the root are minus the partial characteristic derivatives divided by its nonzero x derivative. Evaluating characteristic(J(L)) holds the root argument derivative at zero, as required for those partials.

The normalized right and left slow eigenvectors solve the fast two-by-two block equations with first component one. The block determinant is checked through interval division; left-right normalization gives the rank-one spectral projector.
With right slow vector(1,v), H=F-vb acts on quotient coordinates W=(-v,I). The identities WR=HW, WQ=W and Q[:,fast]W=Q give exp(Rt)=exp(lambda t)P+Q[:,fast]exp(Ht)W.

Detailed balance makes all actual eigenvalues real and diagonalizable. The fast half-gap squared is nonnegative; explicitly checking a+sqrt(d2)<lambda isolates the slow mode from both fast eigenvalues.

The induced infinity norm of diagonal exponentials on a segment is bounded by exp(segment*max Dii). Each n-insertion simplex has volume1/n!, giving omitted norm<=exp(m)(exp(c)-1-c).

Differentiating a term contributes either a diagonal derivative with total segment length one, or one of n off-diagonal derivatives. Summing n>=2 gives exp(m)[norm(Dprime)(exp(c)-1-c)+norm(Cprime)(exp(c)-1)].

The code adds symmetric bounds of these sizes to every matrix entry and derivative. It differentiates the retained formulas by interval AD and includes parameter dependence of the block transformation separately.

The binary KL formula q phi(d/q)+(1-q)phi(-d/(1-q)) is exact because linear terms cancel. Adding basin KL and mass-weighted conditional KL yields the full four-state KL by its chain rule.

Temperature derivatives of a Gibbs distribution are qi(Ei-U)/T^2 and qi[((Ei-U)^2-Var(E))/T^4-2(Ei-U)/T^3]. Their masses vanish, so the same reduced semigroup propagates them without adding equilibrium.

The reconstructed evolved derivatives give D_T=sum pprime log(p/pi) and D_TT=sum[(pprime)^2/p+psecond log(p/pi)]. Interval AD through those expressions also supplies parameter gradients and the next thermal derivatives needed by centered bounds.

acceptance_and_coverage: Distance acceptance requires both0.9 Dc-Dh>=0 and Dc>=.001 throughout the cell. Interval comparisons use the conservative endpoints of the exact decimal thresholds.

Time-margin acceptance concerns F=Dc(u)-Dh(.95u) when Dc lies in the threshold band. The derivative with respect to u of the hot term is explicitly multiplied by.95 after evaluation; physical-parameter derivatives already include the fixed factor in the input time.

Whole-cell exclusion is allowed only if the enclosing cold distance interval is disjoint from the threshold band. Otherwise F+alpha(Dc-.01) or F+alpha(.001-Dc)>=0 with alpha>=0 implies F>=0 on the band.
Heuristic choices of alpha are finite nonnegative binary constants. Every chosen expression is reevaluated with interval arithmetic; the heuristic estimate itself supplies no proof.

When selected-expression partial derivatives have fixed sign over the whole cell, its minimum lies on the corresponding face. The face evaluates exactly the same selected multiplier expression; a face outside the threshold band never excludes the original cell.

The hot-derivative obligation uses the analogous band multipliers on -D_T and whole-cell hot-distance exclusion. It requires nonnegativity, not strict negativity of D_T, which is sufficient for the root monotonicity reduction.
